guarantees.claim: On reset (negedge rst_ni), status_alert_recov_ctrl_update_err is cleared to 0.
When alert_recov_operation is high (and no reset), status_alert_recov_ctrl_update_err is set to 1.
When err_processed is high and alert_recov_operation is low (and no reset), status_alert_recov_ctrl_update_err is cleared to 0.
When none of the active conditions apply (rst_ni high, alert_recov_operation low, err_processed low), status_alert_recov_ctrl_update_err retains its previous value.

uncertain_points.claim: If alert_recov_operation and err_processed are both high on the same cycle, the set takes priority because of the else-if structure. It is unclear whether the design expects this case or whether the driving logic prevents it.
uncertain_points.risk: A simultaneous assert could prevent the flag from being cleared, leading to a stale or spurious error indication if the clearing intent is missed.

uncertain_points.claim: If err_processed is never asserted after alert_recov_operation, the flag remains high indefinitely. External logic must eventually generate err_processed to clear the flag, or the flag could become permanently stuck.
uncertain_points.cond: alert_recov_operation occurred but err_processed never asserted
uncertain_points.risk: A permanently stuck high flag could mask subsequent alert events or cause incorrect recovery handling.
